In [[mathematics]], a '''piecewise isometry''' is a [[dynamical system]] that consists of finitely many [[Euclidean isometry|Euclidean isometries]] acting in different places, including [[rotation (mathematics)|rotations]], [[Translation (geometry)|translations]], and [[reflection (mathematics)|reflections]].<ref name="Goetz2003">{{cite book |last1=Goetz |first1=Arek |title=Fractals in Graz 2001 |chapter=Piecewise Isometries — an Emerging Area of Dynamical Systems |date=2003 |pages=135–144 |doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-8014-5_4 |isbn=978-3-0348-9403-6 }}</ref> Piecewise isometries are higher-dimensional generalizations of [[interval exchange transformation]]s; the theory has applications in [[outer billiards]], [[digital filter]]s, and [[granular mixing]].<ref name="Goetz2003"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Smith |first1=Lauren D. |last2=Umbanhowar |first2=Paul B. |last3=Lueptow |first3=Richard M. |last4=Ottino |first4=Julio M. |title=The geometry of cutting and shuffling: An outline of possibilities for piecewise isometries |journal=Physics Reports |date=2019 |volume=802 |pages=1–22 |doi=10.1016/j.physrep.2019.01.003 |bibcode=2019PhR...802....1S }}</ref>
